subject.title: [Feature]: Add a visible browser panel to the Control UI for login handoff and browser management

question: What security and ownership boundary should the Control UI browser-login handoff use before implementation?
rationale: The issue is valid, but automation cannot safely choose whether this belongs as first-party core UI or plugin-contributed UI, nor what browser-state exposure and write-action policy maintainers want.

options.title: Admin read-only-first handoff panel
options.body: Add a secured operator/admin-scoped panel that shows status, tabs, target context, and safe preview information by default while requiring explicit user actions for navigation, clicks, credential entry, and resume.

options.title: Wait for plugin UI entry points
options.body: Defer the browser-specific panel until the generic plugin UI entry-point contract lands, then implement browser management as a browser-plugin-owned tab under that reviewed boundary.

options.title: Defer browser handoff UI
options.body: Keep CLI/RPC/browser doctor workflows for now and revisit the visible handoff surface when browser-preview work becomes a product priority.

recommendation.title: Admin read-only-first handoff panel
recommendation.body: Add a secured operator/admin-scoped panel that shows status, tabs, target context, and safe preview information by default while requiring explicit user actions for navigation, clicks, credential entry, and resume.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from the issue discussion, browser.request/security history, and current plugin-tab UI plumbing.
